chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Takbeer during the days of Tashreeq is from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Asr prayer of the last day of Tashreeq, if you stay in Mina; and if you leave, there is no Takbeer upon you.

And the Takbeer is that you say: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. And to Allah belongs the praise. Allah is the Greatest for what He guided us [to]. Allah is the Greatest for what He provided us from the beasts of grazing livestock. And the praise is to Allah for what He tried us with.'

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashreeq: The 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah following Eid al-Adha.
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: Takbeer: The act of saying 'Allah is the Greatest', a ritual declaration of praise.
key_terms.بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعَامِ: Bahimat al-An'am: Beasts of grazing livestock (camels, cattle, sheep, goats) used for sacrifice.
key_terms.بِمِنًى: Bil-Mina: In the valley of Mina, near Mecca, where pilgrims stay during Hajj.
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Yawm al-Nahr: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah, Eid al-Adha).

ai.seo_question: What is the correct time and text for reciting Takbeer during the Days of Tashreeq in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific temporal boundaries for the Takbeer al-Tashreeq, linking the ritual obligation directly to the pilgrim's physical presence in Mina, a key element of Shia fiqh regarding Hajj rituals. The detailed formula highlights the dual themes of divine guidance (Hidayah) and material provision (Rizq), reflecting the Shia emphasis on gratitude for both spiritual and worldly blessings during the Eid al-Adha celebrations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al father Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The Takbeer during the days of Al-Tashreek (11th, 12th & 13th Zilhajj), from Salaat Al-Zohr on the day of the sacrifice up to Salaat Al-Asr from the last day of Al-Tashreek, if you stay in Mina; and if you exit, so there is no exclaiming of the Takbeer upon you.

And the Takbeer is that you should be saying, ‘‘Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description)! Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description)! There is no god except for Allahazwj, and Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description). Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description). And for Allahazwj is the Praise. Allahazwj is the Greatest upon what Allahazwj having Guided us. Allahazwj is the Greatest upon having Graced us over the animals, the cattle, and the Praise is for Allahazwj upon having Tried us’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Takbir in the days of Tashriq is from Salat (prayer) of al-Zuhr on the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah) to Salat (prayer) of al-‘Asr of the last day of Tashriq, if you remain in Mina’. If you leave Mina 5 you are not obligated for anything in this matter.

In Takhir say, ’Allah is great beyond description, Allah is great beyond description. No one deserves worship except Allah. Allah is great beyond description. Allah is great beyond description. All praise belongs to Allah. Allah is great beyond description. Allah is great beyond description as He has given us the cattle and all praise belongs to Allah for His testing and trials for us.’”
